archetypes.name: risk-integration
archetypes.rationale: The scout manifest path is now a required flag in launch-codex-implement.sh; if any caller site hasn't been updated the whole Codex implement path will exit 2 before launching.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the new --scout-manifest-path required-flag loop in scripts/launch-codex-implement.sh: trace every caller of this launcher (step2-implement.sh and anything that shells to it) to verify each call site now supplies --scout-manifest-path. Also inspect the parse-drafter-output.py fourth-argument change: any existing call site that passes only three positional args will now write the scout candidate to the wrong path or fail. Check both launch-claude-drafter.sh and launch-codex-drafter.sh for cleanup-on-failure paths that might leave _scout_candidate or _scout_filtered temp files behind when early-exit branches are taken before the rm -f lines. Verify that SCOUT_WRITTEN and SCOUT_FAIL_REASON are correctly initialized before write_status_file in all launchers' pre-launch error paths, since write_status_file now references ${SCOUT_WRITTEN:-false} unconditionally. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: Two behavioral changes unrelated to the plan's two stated bugs: the default coder priority was swapped (codex now wins over cursor) and the SECURITY.md mutual-exclusion claim between --emergency and --merge was reversed.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the coder-priority swap in python/bootstrap.py where codex is now preferred over cursor when both are available, and check whether the parallel swap in test_bootstrap.py (the parametrize matrix entry '(empty, true, true)' now expects codex) is the only place this assumption is encoded — look for any other callers or docs that mention the old cursor-first behavior. Separately, SECURITY.md now says '/implement --emergency and --merge are compatible' replacing the old mutual-exclusion statement; verify that skills/implement/SKILL.md, the admission gate in python/admission.py, and any bootstrap logic that handled the incompatibility are actually consistent with this new claim, or whether the SECURITY.md prose was updated without matching code changes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
